Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Work & responsibility · Money, work & business

earn verb

get money by working

also earn a living, make a living, make money, earnings, how much do you earn?

classical

Cic. Rosc. Com. 28: merēre per sē nōn amplius poterant duodecim aeris
Suet. Cal. 40 (Lewis & Short)

mereō, merēre, meruī, meritum

verb, second conjugation

earn (pay, a sum)

Of wages and pay; stīpendia merēre is to serve as a soldier. The deponent mereor is more often “deserve” (see earn, deserve).

Examples

  • lānā ac tēlā vīctum quaeritāns

    earning her living by spinning and weavingTer. And. 75

  • nam illa membra merēre per sē nōn amplius poterant duodecim aeris

    for that body on its own could not earn more than twelve assesCic. Rosc. Com. 28

Other words

  • vīctum quaeritāre — earn a living

    verb phrase · also used · classical · Ter. And. 75: lānā ac tēlā vīctum quaeritāns; Traupman 102, 162

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    quaeritō is ante-classical (Lewis & Short); Cato says rem quaerere for making money (Agr. praef. 1).

  • quaestum facere — make a living (Traupman)

    verb phrase · avoid · classical · Traupman 102

    Used absolutely in comedy of a prostitute’s trade (Ter. Haut. 640: utī quaestum faceret; Lewis & Short s.v. quaestus).

See also income, job, earn, position.

SourcesLewis & Short: mereo · Lewis & Short: quaerito · Lewis & Short: quaestus
